newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia manufacturers seen boosting output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia manufacturers seen boosting output.

text.p: Australia's soon-to-be-released national manufacturing survey for the December quarter shows the first major rise in manufacturers' production forecasts in 18 months, the nation's manufacturing lobby said on Tuesday.
The Australian Chamber of Manufacturers said its survey of around 800 firms, to be released in a few days, showed a net 17 percent planned to increase production in the March quarter.
"It's the first time it's ticked up in the last six or seven quarters," chamber chief executive Allan Handberg told Reuters, adding that it was the first rise of any substance.
"There's been a couple of little blips (previously)," he said.
The net balance of firms that boosted production in the December quarter was 22 percent, a chamber spokesman said, adding that manufacturing normally picked up around Christmas.
Handberg criticised the Reserve Bank for moving too cautiously on interest rates, saying the latest survey results were merely proof that manufacturing activity had bottomed.
"It's not had an impact," he said of the central bank's move to cut the official cash rate three times by half a percentage point since July.

"They should have done a full whack back in mid-year because the economy had been slowing already for four or five quarters at that stage. All the signs were there. Our complaint is that they are reactive rather then anticipating."
Handberg was speaking after at a breakfast address to the chamber by Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer.
